title: Unique minimum-area Reuleaux polygons of prescribed unit width and inradius below one half
source_title: Body of constant width with minimal area in a given annulus
author: Antoine Henrot; Ilaria Lucardesi
difficulty_reason: A fixed-inradius constraint prevents the usual unconstrained Blaschke deformation argument from identifying the area minimiser directly. The author proves rigidity of the admissible clusters, derives their exact area formula and strict interior concavity, and uses the constrained arc-count optimisation to exclude competing polygon configurations. This geometric reduction and analytic sign construction establish the unique polygon optimiser without relying on the separate density claim for arbitrary constant-width bodies.
source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.150

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Theorem4.1 in the class of Reuleaux polygons with at most2N+1 sides, inradius1−1/sqrt(3)≤r<1/2 and width1; uniqueness only up to rigid motion within this polygon class. Full shape derivative, rigidity and analytic concavity core included. No extension to arbitrary constant-width bodies via the separate unproved fixed-inradius density step in Theorem1.2. Bounded display notes:4.4 second derivative vanishes at h=0, while strict concavity on the interval is established by negativity in its interior;3.8 printed derivative comparison has its endpoint reversed, but explicit derivative and the stated fixed r range directly give positivity without any new geometric argument. Final24 arc-count sentence prints N(r)−2 where its displayed expression gives2N(r)−2; exact optimizer Definition3.10 and statement4.1 consistently have2N(r)+1 sides. Explicit polynomial sign checks in the authored concavity construction are bounded ancillary verification, not omitted new core.
